title: Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 Adds Durable and Verifiable Execution for AI Agents
gist: Diagrid's Catalyst 2.0 adds Dapr-based checkpointing and cryptographic attestation to ten agent frameworks (LangGraph, AWS Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, etc.), targeting the durability/audit gap in agentic AI infrastructure, but its performance claims are unverifiable and the security guarantee only covers record integrity, not correctness of agent decisions.

themes.theme: Durability layer as an agentic-AI infrastructure land-grab

insights.claim: Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 adds durable, checkpointed execution and cryptographic history verification across ten agent frameworks at once, including LangGraph, LangGraph Deep Agents, Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, Dapr Agents, AWS Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Managed Agents, CrewAI and Pydantic AI.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Broad framework coverage in one release signals a bid to become the horizontal infrastructure layer for agent reliability before any single framework wins the agent-orchestration war; watch whether hyperscalers or framework vendors build this natively instead, which would commoditize Diagrid's wedge.

insights.claim: Catalyst represents model and tool calls as durable workflow activities so that an interrupted multi-step agent run can resume without repeating already-completed (and already-paid-for) model calls.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: For any business running long, expensive multi-step LLM agent chains, uncheckpointed retries silently multiply token spend on failure; call-granularity durability is a direct lever on effective inference cost at scale.
insights.quote: a long multi-step run fails late in the sequence and, without checkpointing at call granularity, the retry re-pays for every model call already completed
insights.locator: The failure mode this targets is a familiar one

insights.claim: Catalyst is not a first-mover in agent durability: LangGraph already offers checkpoint-based persistence and resumable execution via its Agent Server, and Temporal and Restate already provide replay/journal-based durable execution that can host agent workflows.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The differentiation claim rests on breadth (one model spanning many frameworks, call-level not graph-level granularity) rather than novelty, meaning competitive moat depends on multi-framework lock-in effects, not unique technology.
insights.quote: Catalyst is neither the first durability option for these frameworks nor a new entrant to a thin market.
insights.locator: Catalyst is neither the first durability option

themes.theme: Cryptographic attestation for agent audit trails

insights.claim: Dapr 1.18 verifies agent workflow history by hashing batches of workflow events, chaining each digest to the prior signature, and signing with the Dapr sidecar's SPIFFE-based identity, letting receivers validate history outside the application that produced it via the Dapr Sentry trust anchor.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: This is a tamper-evidence mechanism for regulated or high-stakes agent deployments (finance, healthcare) where auditors need proof an agent's action log wasn't altered after the fact -- a compliance feature that could become a sales differentiator as agentic AI regulation tightens.
insights.locator: The verification model comes from Dapr 1.18.

insights.claim: Signing is disabled by default in Dapr 1.18, requires mTLS (daprd refuses to start if signing is on and mTLS is off), and is a one-way, non-retroactive decision per workflow -- existing history can't be signed after the fact and in-flight unsigned workflows must finish or be purged before enabling it broadly.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Operational friction (opt-in flag, mTLS dependency, no retroactive coverage) means real-world adoption of verifiable audit trails will lag the marketing message; enterprises evaluating this for compliance should budget migration/rollout time, not assume day-one coverage.
insights.quote: toggling signing for a workflow already running is a verification error, so in-flight unsigned workflows must complete or be purged before enabling it more widely
insights.locator: Teams should note that signing is disabled by default

insights.claim: Cryptographic attestation proves only the integrity and provenance of recorded history -- it does not prove an agent made a correct decision, a tool returned accurate data, or that every external side effect was captured.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Buyers should not conflate 'verifiable execution' with 'trustworthy AI output' -- this closes a forensic/audit gap, not a correctness/safety gap, so agent-quality risk (hallucination, bad tool calls) remains fully unaddressed by this product category.
insights.quote: Cryptographic attestation proves the integrity and provenance of recorded history, not that an agent made a correct decision, a tool returned accurate data, or every external side effect was captured.

insights.claim: Yaron Schneider, Diagrid co-founder/CTO and chair of the Agentic AI Foundation's Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, frames the core customer need as organizations wanting 'proof of what happened' when agents call tools or delegate work.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Signals that enterprise agent adoption is increasingly gated on auditability rather than capability -- a governance/compliance bottleneck, which favors vendors selling trust infrastructure alongside or ahead of raw agent capability.
insights.locator: Yaron Schneider, Diagrid co-founder and CTO

insights.claim: Diagrid claims Catalyst delivers up to ten times the performance of open-source Dapr and supports millions of concurrent agent workflows, but does not specify whether the multiple refers to throughput, workflow starts per second, or latency, nor the workload, hardware, or Dapr configuration used for comparison.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Unfalsifiable benchmark claims are a red flag for diligence; investors and technical buyers should discount headline performance multipliers from vendor announcements until independently reproducible methodology is published.
insights.quote: The announcement does not say whether that multiple refers to throughput, workflow starts per second or latency, nor which workload, hardware or Dapr configuration it was measured against, so the comparison cannot be independently assessed.
insights.locator: Diagrid claims Catalyst can deliver up to ten times

insights.claim: Diagrid's commercial model spans a free cloud tier, dedicated-cloud and bring-your-own-cloud plans priced by concurrent workflows, plus a custom-quoted Enterprise Server edition for on-premise and air-gapped deployments.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Usage-based pricing tied to concurrent workflows means Diagrid's revenue scales directly with enterprise agent deployment volume, making it a leveraged proxy bet on enterprise agentic-AI adoption rather than a fixed-fee tools vendor.

insights.claim: Optics manufacturer ZEISS Group is the only named early adopter of Catalyst 2.0, with its head of end-to-end core application engineering saying it provides a stable foundation amid a rapidly evolving landscape of AI models and frameworks.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A single named reference customer in a non-tech industrial vertical suggests the product is early-stage in enterprise validation; investors should treat this as a pilot-stage signal, not proof of broad product-market fit.
insights.quote: Catalyst provides the stable foundation we can rely on
insights.locator: Named early adoption is limited so far
